name: Amazon Route 53
description: Highly available and scalable DNS web service with health checking and traffic routing policies.
limitations: not a substitute for a CDN or load balancer
DNS caching can delay failover propagation

name: Amazon CloudFront
description: Global content delivery network (CDN) that caches content at edge locations close to users.
limitations: cache invalidation adds operational overhead
not useful for highly dynamic, non-cacheable content

name: Amazon API Gateway
description: Managed service for creating, publishing, and securing REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs at scale.
limitations: added latency vs direct ALB
cost can grow at very high request volumes

name: Application Load Balancer
description: Layer 7 load balancer that routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic across multiple targets and supports path/host-based rules.
common_use_cases: distributing traffic across containers or EC2
limitations: layer 7 only (no raw TCP/UDP)
regional, not global, without CloudFront in front

name: Amazon ECS
description: Fully managed container orchestration service, usable with the serverless Fargate launch type or self-managed EC2.
limitations: less portable than Kubernetes
fewer third-party ecosystem tools than EKS

name: Amazon EKS
description: Managed Kubernetes control plane for running containerized workloads with the full Kubernetes ecosystem.
limitations: higher operational complexity than ECS
steeper learning curve
control plane cost

name: AWS Lambda
description: Serverless compute that runs code in response to events without provisioning or managing servers.
limitations: execution time limits
cold starts
not ideal for long-running or stateful workloads

name: Amazon EC2
description: Resizable virtual machines with full control over the operating system and runtime.
limitations: requires patching and OS management
manual scaling setup via Auto Scaling Groups

name: Amazon RDS
description: Managed relational database service supporting engines like PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server.
limitations: vertical scaling limits for writes
cross-region replication adds latency

name: Amazon Aurora
description: AWS-built MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible relational database with distributed, self-healing storage.
common_use_cases: global applications via Aurora Global Database
limitations: higher cost than standard RDS
still bound by relational write-scaling limits

name: Amazon DynamoDB
description: Fully managed, serverless key-value and document NoSQL database with single-digit millisecond latency.
limitations: limited query flexibility vs SQL
requires careful key/partition design
complex multi-item transactions

name: Amazon ElastiCache
description: Managed in-memory caching service supporting Redis and Memcached.
limitations: cache invalidation complexity
additional infrastructure to manage and monitor

name: Amazon S3
description: Durable, highly available object storage for any amount of data.
limitations: not a file system (object storage semantics)
eventual consistency considerations for some access patterns

name: Amazon SQS
description: Fully managed message queuing service for decoupling and scaling microservices.
limitations: no native pub/sub fan-out (needs SNS)
message ordering requires FIFO queues with lower throughput

name: Amazon SNS
description: Fully managed pub/sub messaging service for fanning out notifications to multiple subscribers.
strengths: integrates with SQS, Lambda, email, SMS
limitations: no message retention/replay on its own
not designed for complex event routing rules

name: Amazon EventBridge
description: Serverless event bus for building event-driven architectures with content-based routing rules.
limitations: not designed for very high-throughput streaming (use Kinesis)
at-least-once delivery semantics

name: Amazon VPC
description: Isolated virtual network within AWS for launching resources with full control over IP ranges, subnets, and routing.
strengths: supports fine-grained security groups and NACLs
limitations: misconfiguration can expose resources publicly
adds design complexity vs default networking

name: AWS IAM
description: Identity and access management service for controlling authentication and authorization to AWS resources.
strengths: deeply integrated across all AWS services
limitations: overly permissive policies are a common misconfiguration risk
policy complexity at scale

name: AWS WAF
description: Web application firewall that protects APIs and web apps from common exploits at the edge (with CloudFront/ALB).
strengths: managed rule groups for OWASP Top 10
integrates with CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway
limitations: requires rule tuning to avoid false positives
does not protect against all application-logic flaws

name: Amazon CloudWatch
description: Monitoring and observability service for metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards.
strengths: native integration with every AWS service
limitations: log storage costs grow quickly at scale
less rich querying than dedicated observability platforms

name: AWS Secrets Manager
description: Managed service for storing, rotating, and retrieving secrets such as database credentials and API keys.
limitations: per-secret cost at scale
requires application-level integration to fetch secrets

name: AWS KMS
description: Managed service for creating and controlling encryption keys used to encrypt data across AWS services.
limitations: API request cost at very high volume
key policy misconfiguration can lock out access

name: AWS Auto Scaling
description: Automatically adjusts compute capacity (EC2, ECS) based on demand or schedules.
common_use_cases: cost optimization by scaling down off-peak
limitations: scaling lag during sudden spikes
requires stateless, horizontally scalable workloads

name: AWS Backup
description: Centralized backup service for automating and managing backups across AWS services.
limitations: storage cost for long retention
restore time varies by data volume

name: AWS X-Ray
description: Distributed tracing service for analyzing and debugging requests across microservices.
limitations: requires instrumentation in application code
sampling can miss rare edge cases

name: AWS Shield
description: Managed DDoS protection service, with a Standard tier free for all customers and an Advanced tier for enhanced protection.
strengths: automatic mitigation of common network-layer attacks
Advanced tier includes cost protection and 24/7 DRT support
limitations: Advanced tier has significant fixed cost
does not replace application-layer security controls
